title: Agents Need Receipts, Not More Tool Calls - Armanas Povilionis, Alithea Bio
talk_summary: The speaker presents Froglet, an open protocol for agents to discover external services, transact, and receive signed verifiable receipts across organizational boundaries. The demo shows a Froglet node exposed via MCP, with keypair-signed artifact chains and async deal IDs, but most claims are protocol vision rather than measured production results.

takeaways.what_they_do: Each Froglet node has a keypair and signs every artifact in an execution chain; a receipt is valid only if the whole chain is untampered.
takeaways.evidence_quote: everything is being signed in a chain, and the chain is only valid if all data points are not tampered with.

takeaways.technique: MCP service boundary for remote execution
takeaways.what_they_do: Froglet is exposed as an MCP server/plugin so the agent calls a service with a compact payload; payment, execution environment, and receipt stay below the LLM context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: not shoving everything into a uh LLM context. It just has a services that it needs to interact.

takeaways.what_they_do: Requester gets a deal ID immediately and polls until the remote service finishes, rather than blocking on a long tool call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I take a for command for loop to actually wait for it

takeaways.what_they_do: Requests carry schema, target service, provider, and input, enabling discovery and direct execution without bespoke integration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: payload which includes many things including schema, what kind of service I'm targeting, also which provider, and finally what input
